cases.name: Google Eemshaven
cases.geography_note: Eemshaven from S04; Het Hogeland municipality inferred from locality and S15 municipal context, not a cadastral match.
cases.latest_source_note: Latest dated site-specific item is secondary (S22); owner location page S04 undated. S15 is unattributed local context.
cases.angle: Test whether a proven operator capability can become a site-specific commitment.
cases.next: Verify the serving node and contractual headroom, then obtain a time-stamped workload-reduction profile.
cases.stop: Do not recommend a flexible connection without the site's import rights and tolerable interruption envelope.
cases.scenario: Workload shifting is a hypothesis informed by operator-level evidence, not a verified site capability.

cases.name: Google Winschoten
cases.latest_source_note: S06 is undated; construction milestone discrepancy is retained.
cases.angle: Separate documented cooling and solar design from unproven electrical flexibility.
cases.next: Obtain the connection agreement, solar output profile and workload scheduling constraints.
cases.stop: Do not treat solar panels or air cooling as evidence of firm capacity during a constrained hour.
cases.scenario: Test flexible demand plus controllable supply; solar contribution during the event remains unknown.

cases.name: NorthC Groningen 1 & 2
cases.geography_note: S08 lists the Groningen address; campus aggregate retained.
cases.status: Operating locations described by current owner listing
cases.latest_source_note: S18 dates an activity notification, not commissioning. Owner capacity/technology pages remain undated.
cases.angle: Investigate whether emergency hydrogen equipment could support an agreed grid service.
cases.next: Check operating permits, usable hydrogen inventory, reserve policy and customer service obligations.
cases.stop: Do not count emergency reserves as routinely dispatchable generation without permission and availability evidence.
cases.scenario: Use of backup for routine congestion events is an explicit assumption requiring validation.

cases.name: Google Westpoort
cases.geography_note: S19 identifies Westpoort, municipality Groningen. Distinct from NorthC at the same business park.
cases.status: Construction announced 2024; planned grid connection discussed May 2026
cases.latest_source_note: Month precision; opening / commissioning not established in this review.
cases.angle: Examine whether operational flexibility could change a documented grid-delivery dependency.
cases.next: Confirm the Westpoort–Vierverlaten project match, delivery milestones and whether a staged or flexible offer is relevant.
cases.stop: Do not assume that a planned connection is delayed, unavailable or eligible for accelerated access.
cases.scenario: A flexible connection is a comparison to investigate, not an option known to have been offered.

assumptions.text: Selected locations illustrate different evidence types; selection does not establish that they are the most promising Dutch projects.
Scenario options are hypothetical counterfactuals for existing locations or a future expansion, not existing offers.
No actual financial, capacity, emissions or time-to-power outcomes are calculated.
Source-confirmed means the source makes the statement; owner statements are not independent engineering verification.
Unknown means not established in the reviewed source set, not absent in reality.
Editable scenario notes are user assumptions only and never alter the evidence record.
A zero event energy gap would not by itself establish net system benefit; rebound, recharge, fuel and location must also be tested.
National expansion uses purposive geographic and evidence-type coverage, not a census. Eight provinces are represented; missing provinces do not imply no data centres.
